result.stdout:
Description:
  Azure Service Bus CLI and terminal UI: browse, peek, retry and send messages

Usage:
  azsb [command] [options]

Options:
  -s, --subscription <subscription>  Azure subscription to start in, by name or ID; emulator for the local emulator
  -n, --namespace <namespace>        Namespace of that subscription to open, by name or host name; needs --subscription
  -o, --open <open>                  Queue, topic or topic/subscription of that namespace to open, by exact name; /dlq or /active picks the tab. Or a list: queues, topics or subscriptions. Needs --namespace
  -t, --theme <theme>                Colors for a dark or light terminal background: auto (default; COLORFGBG, else dark), dark or light; overrides ui.theme
  -?, -h, --help                     Show help and usage information
  --version                          Show version information

Commands:
  run                                             Open the terminal UI (the default command)
  check                                           Check that a namespace can be used from here: Azure sign-in, DNS, the AMQP port and a peek
  list <queues|topics|subscriptions>              List queues and subscriptions (or one kind) with their message counts
  peek <entity>                                   Print messages of a queue or subscription without changing them
  retry <entity>                                  Send dead-lettered messages back to their queue or topic and remove them from the dead-letter queue
  delete <entity>                                 Delete dead-lettered messages by message ID or sequence number
  purge <entity>                                  Delete every message of a queue or subscription, or of its dead-letter queue
  send <entity>                                   Send a new message to a queue or topic
  config <get|list|path|set|unset> <key> <value>  Read and write settings in the config file, like git config:
                                                    get <key>: print a value, exit code 1 when unset; unset <ke
[truncated]

Description:
  Print messages of a queue or subscription without changing them

Usage:
  azsb peek <entity> [options]

Arguments:
  <entity>  Queue or topic/subscription; topic/Subscriptions/subscription and a /$DeadLetterQueue suffix work too

Options:
  --dlq                              The dead-letter queue
  --max <max>                        Most messages to peek [default: 20]
  --from-sequence <from-sequence>    Peek from this sequence number on
  --full                             Print whole bodies; longer ones are cut at 4 KB otherwise
  -s, --subscription <subscription>  Azure subscription, by name or ID; emulator for the local emulator. Default: the Azure CLI's current subscription
  -n, --namespace <namespace>        Namespace, by name, host name or a pattern with * that matches one. Default: the subscription's only namespace
  --json                             Write JSON to standard output
  -?, -h, --help                     Show help and usage information

Description:
  Send dead-lettered messages back to their queue or topic and remove them from the dead-letter queue

Usage:
  azsb retry <entity> [options]

Arguments:
  <entity>  Queue or topic/subscription; topic/Subscriptions/subscription and a /$DeadLetterQueue suffix work too

Options:
  --message-id <message-id>          Message ID to act on, repeatable; every message with that ID
  --sequence <sequence>              Sequence number to act on, repeatable
  --all                              Every message among the first --limit
  --limit <limit>                    How many messages from the front to look through [default: 1000]
  --dry-run                          Show which messages match without changing anything
  --confirm <confirm>                The namespace's name: needed for changes in a namespace listed in cli.protect
  -s, --subscription <subscription>  Azure subscription, by name or ID; emulator for the local emulator. Default: the Azure CLI's current subscription
  -n, --namespace <namespace>        Namespace, by name, host name or a pattern with * that matches one. Default: the subscription's only namespace
  --json                             Write JSON to standard output
  -?, -h, --help                     Show help and usage information

result.stdout:
Description:
  Read and write settings in the config file, like git config:
    get <key>: print a value, exit code 1 when unset; unset <key>: remove it
    set <key> <value>: true/false and integers are stored as such, the rest as text
    list [--all]: print key=value lines, secrets masked; path: print the config file's path

Usage:
  azsb config <action> [<key> [<value>]] [options]

Arguments:
  <get|list|path|set|unset>  get, set, unset, list or path
  <key>                      Dotted key, such as ui.theme
  <value>                    Value to set

Options:
  --all           With list: also the known keys that are unset, with their default and description
  -?, -h, --help  Show help and usage information
